# MemoryFeed v0.3.0 — Extractor Reliability

MemoryFeed v0.3.0 focuses on extractor reliability, capture quality, deduplication, and platform-level observability.

This release improves capture stability across Facebook, X/Twitter, YouTube, LinkedIn, and TikTok by standardizing capture payloads, adding selector fallback logic, canonicalizing URLs, improving duplicate detection, and exposing reliability metrics.

## Highlights

- Standardized capture schema:
  - `platform`
  - `canonical_url`
  - `author_name`
  - `text`
  - `media_urls`
  - `post_id`
  - `captured_at`
  - optional `author_handle`, `thumbnail_url`, `source_context`

- Improved platform extractors:
  - Primary selectors plus fallback selectors
  - Graceful degradation when fields are missing
  - `quality_flags` for incomplete captures
  - `capture_debug.selector_used`
  - `missing_fields` tracking

- Better deduplication:
  - New fingerprint strategy based on:
    - canonical URL
    - normalized text
    - author
    - 2-hour time bucket
  - Duplicate skipping during capture/store

- Observability:
  - Structured `capture_attempt` logs
  - Per-platform reliability stats in `/api/stats`
  - Attempts, stored items, duplicates, missing required fields, success rate, and fail rate

- Tests:
  - Added capture reliability tests for five platforms
  - Covered happy path, selector drift, missing author, missing media, and duplicate cases

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` -> 11/11 OK
- `python -m compileall backend memoryfeed tests` -> OK
- `node --check` for main extension JS files -> OK

## Tradeoffs

- Extractors are more resilient, but social platform DOMs can still change.
- URL canonicalization improves dedupe, but platform-specific edge cases may still require follow-up patches.
- Quality flags allow incomplete captures instead of hard failures, which improves recall but requires UI/debug review for low-quality captures.

## Deferred to v0.3.1

- Real-world fixture expansion from saved HTML samples.
- UI panel for capture quality/debug visibility.
- More aggressive media/image deduplication.
- Optional per-platform extractor confidence scoring.
